name: John Howard Adams
personality: Tried to be kind, understanding, generous and demonstrative
notable_stories: Delivered Barbara’s sack lunch to Lowell when he was near Port Townsend on Reserve weekend.
Initially became a 'Catholic of convenience' to simplify marrying a Catholic.
Has maintained a friendship with Kevin Finnegan.
Did not like sharing Barbara with other suitors in Baltimore.
Asked Barbara's father for permission to marry her.
Proposed to Barbara in the basement of her house.
Moved frequently with Barbara during Navy life and later civilian work.
Drove truck for a while after being downsized.
Built a plywood platform over the back seating area for the trip.
Pulled over during Brian's diaper blowout.
Went to Survival School and lost 13 pounds in a week.
Went into the emergency room with Brendan while Barbara waited outside.
Later took Brian to the hospital for his injury.
Reassured Barbara that Brian would be okay.
Provided his own favorite songs list within the artifact.
Blue and Gold admissions officer for USNA
Honeymoon: Drove Annapolis → Pensacola FL for continued flight training
Best Man at wedding: Willie Durkin — John's high school best friend from San Francisco, career SF firefighter, Navy Corpsman at NAS Jacksonville. Died 2021, Alzheimer's complications.

Proposal to Barbara: After the 1968 Army-Navy game, Philadelphia, PA. Conversation-based (no ring, no knee); 'O'Neils, O'Donnels, O'Dells and O'Adams' entourage in hotel room. John subsequently asked Buckey, who replied: 'What makes you think you can support her in the manner she is accustomed on an Ensign's salary in the Navy?' John's starting salary was $345/month plus flight pay.

Engagement ring: 1/2-karat VVS stone bought in Annapolis. Presented to Barbara asleep in the basement of her Baltimore home (Nov 1968). Rating upgraded to 'Flawless' over decades through re-mountings.
Barbara also has a pinky-finger miniature Naval Academy ring with aquamarine stones cut from the same stone as John's Academy ring.
Wedding ring briefly lost playing softball in Port Townsend; replaced by Barbara with a narrower band.
Name origin: John probably after John Kulp (mother's grandfather) or John Wesley Adams (Gen 3). Howard after mother's favorite brother Howard (whose real name was Byron Daniel).
Named 'Howard' after Beryl's favorite brother Byron Daniel 'Howard' Simons (mem).
1952: First big trip — to Okinawa with family.
1954: First family television set; first family car was a used 1949 DeSoto, kept until 1959 departure for Germany.
1964: San Francisco City High School football championship — his school won.
1976: Left active duty, joined Navy Reserves as XO, Aviation Maintenance Division, NAS Whidbey Island.
1978: Transitioned to civilian paper industry (engineering, project management, logistics).
1980: Father George Francis Adams Sr. died.
1995: Left Crown (Crown Zellerbach / Crown Pacific); moved to Redding, CA.

NOTE: This source again reports Beryl's death as 1999 (memoir ~p.136: 'would have turned 80 that Christmas Day'). User has previously confirmed 1998-08-01 as correct canonical date — maintaining 1998. Both memoir sources (this + Adams_Direct_Line) report 1999.
2009: Retired at age 62.
Present (2026): Lives between Ridgefield WA and Englewood CO.
Navy call sign: 'Quincy' — but not routinely used as a nickname.

Mid-air collision off USS Ranger: A-6 Intruder struck by F-4 Phantom wingman whose squadron commander had crossed through the carrier's landing pattern. Cockpit fire; aircraft tumbled. John ejected, failed to release parachute on water entry, pulled underwater twice, finally activated strobe light on helmet, picked up within a minute. Bombardier also ejected — cracked neck, more severely burned. (Memoir p.99-102.)
First boss in civilian world: Lowell Tiller, a consummate Mechanical Engineer; Lowell died early from MS. His wife Lillian and Barbara are close friends to this day.
On August 14, 2021, met a 60-year-old cousin for the very first time.
Applied to all service academies; originally received West Point appointment but requested Annapolis as first choice. Father (in South Korea) was somewhat surprised.
Father's advice staying at USNA: 'Well, if you do that, what do you think you'll do with yourself?' — kept John from leaving halfway through Plebe Year.

Career: State of New Mexico school construction financing in Crownpoint, NM. Position came through son Brendan, who was working for Gerald Martin General Contractor and introduced a State of New Mexico representative to John — John was hired as construction manager for public schools in the north-central part of the state.
Grew up at the Presidio in San Francisco, where his father was a military police officer, and went to high school with O.J. Simpson.
In summer 2010 John was about to take a trip and was mainly interested in the family's Scottish connection. His brother George sent him material on Gavin Hamilton and Robert Burns.
John and Barbara travelled to Scotland with his sister Trudy in 2010.
The family flew home from Frankfurt to New York on a 707 in 1962, picked up a new Dodge and drove across the country by a southern route.

After John finished 4th grade in 1958, the family spent about a month camping across the country from Pasco through Idaho and South Dakota to Georgia, seeing Coeur d'Alene, Mount Rushmore, Yellowstone and the Smoky Mountains; it was the longest stretch of daily time the children ever had with their father.

While living in Germany John first skied in Switzerland, saw the Passion Play at Oberammergau, toured East Berlin before the Wall was built, spent two weeks on the Spanish Riviera, and as a Boy Scout visited Great Britain.
In high school John rode his 15-speed French touring bike from San Francisco to the Russian River and camped on property owned by Mike Remy's family.

John began playing baseball at 7, often on more than one team at once, and stopped after his second year of college; at 15-16 he played on three Bay Area teams and was named league MVP playing catcher and pitcher.
John played center on the 1964 San Francisco City champion high school football team and was named to the All-City team; the team played against future stars O.J. Simpson and Mike Holmgren.

On his summer cruise out of Norfolk, John's ship collided with a fleet tug playing an enemy ship in a war-at-sea exercise; it went into dry dock in Baltimore, Barbara's home town, so he spent most weekends that summer with her.
John bought a car over Christmas break of his senior year, against Academy rules, and kept it hidden; most weekends Barbara came to Annapolis or he went to Baltimore.
A few people called John 'Howie', from his middle name, but it never lasted because the family moved so often.

John never golfed with his father, joking that golf wasn't a sport because you didn't tape your ankles, but took it up with his father's clubs; he played Pebble Beach twice in the late 1980s, made a hole-in-one in a 2001 company tournament at Heron Lakes Golf Course in Portland, OR, and was once paired with Cheech Marin at the Presidio course.

John's lasting high school friends included Susie Miller, Kendall Price and Mark Peterson, who followed him to the Naval Academy; he spent a week with Susie's family on Lake Michigan in summer 1967 and took her to that year's Army-Navy Game.
Plebe Year was the worst year of his life: he was hazed constantly and fought to keep a C average, since anything lower meant probation or dismissal.

Once during the engagement Barbara took off her ring outside a movie theater, put it in John's shirt pocket and said she didn't think she wanted to go through with it; later that evening she took it back out of his pocket.
He still has the original Navy 'Wings of Gold' that Barbara pinned on him when he earned them as a carrier pilot.

The Rolex his parents gave him for his 1965 high-school graduation vanished in about 1973; a couple of years later friends in the Philippines mailed it back after finding it behind the cushions of a sofa set they had bought from John and Barbara. A jeweler later found it was made in 1958, so his father probably bought it in Korea.
He was offered the job of Mill Manager in Carthage, New York, when Brian was about to start his senior year of high school and Brendan his freshman year, and turned it down for the family's sake.
His mother taught him to iron and to cook when he was in about seventh grade; he has done most of the family's ironing ever since and cooks most evening meals in retirement.

After his father died, his mother let the children choose keepsakes and John took his father's pocket knife. He later lost it, Brendan tried to replace it one Christmas, and John finally found the same model.

As Logistics Manager at Wauna he won a weekend at a Columbia Gorge bed and breakfast in a trucking company's golf-tournament drawing; he and Barbara used it for their anniversary and went skiing on Mt. Hood.
Family and friends call John by the pet names "Papa" (to his grandchildren), "Johnboy" and "Best Buddy".
John played organized baseball from age 7 until his second year of college, often on two teams at once, and played every position except first base and the outfield.

When his high-school baseball glove was stolen from the bench during batting practice, John had to buy a replacement from his own savings; he named it "Mr. Mitt," and the glove still survives almost 60 years later in Colorado.
After his father died, John took the gift of his father's golf clubs as a sign to take the game seriously, and went on to play more than a thousand rounds over 40-plus years.
During the pandemic John made hard-bound photo books of their international trips, and he makes a photo book for each grandchild's 16th birthday.
John and Barbara planned a Hawaii vacation for the whole extended family together, and they have made about ten trips to Hawaii, visiting all of the islands.

John and Barbara found the Cadillac Cafe near Lloyd Center in Portland around 1982, just after it opened. They stayed regulars for as long as it existed, and on their 45th anniversary visit, probably in 2015, the owners told them they had sold it.
John and Barbara celebrated their 50th wedding anniversary with the whole family at El Rancho Viejo, their regular Mexican restaurant in Ridgefield.
John became 'Uncle Hims' after his niece Jenny, Chuck's daughter, whom he and Barbara babysat over a long weekend, told her parents tearfully, 'Hims sent me to my room.'

One Saturday night in Kelso, already dressed in suit and tie for a formal dinner, John took the training wheels off Brendan's bike and ran up and down the road with him until he balanced; they still arrived on time.
John collects Hard Rock Cafe T-shirts from locations around the world; on the 2016 South America trip the tour guide let him off at a Hard Rock Cafe to get one.
At the Equator in Ecuador, John was the only one in the tour group who could balance an egg on the head of a nail, earning the title 'Egg Master'.
In Dublin, Barbara saved John's life twice when he looked the wrong way before crossing the street.
In retirement John golfs, goes to the driving range weekly, meets with two coffee groups each week, swims at 24 Hour Fitness, does the food shopping and makes dinner.

Military: John retired from the Navy (Reserves) sometime between ages 41 and 50. (between 1989 and 1998)

Military: His first carrier landings were in a T-28 trainer, flying from NAS Pensacola to the USS Lexington for five landings and five 'deck run' take-offs without a catapult; on the way out the tower had to tell him his wheels were still down. (1969-1970)
Military: In 1972 he was offered the A-7 Corsair first but chose the A-6 Intruder, partly so he would be based in Washington State rather than Jacksonville, Florida.
Military: His squadron on the USS Ranger was VA-145, and his job on the night of the mid-air collision was flying as a tanker, refuelling F-4 Phantoms before their missions.
Military: He counts 25 years in all between the Naval Academy and his Navy career, active and reserve. (1965-c.1990)
Military: John had to eject from two different Navy airplanes, and both aircraft were destroyed; each time investigations cleared him to fly again.

Military: John left active duty for two reasons: long sea tours kept him away from his family, and he feared the ejection investigations on his record would limit his career. He went on to reach the rank of Commander in the Naval Reserve. (1976)
Military: The aircraft carrier John flew from was USS Ranger, hull number CVA-61.
Met Barbara McKeldin in 1967, at the end of John's second (Youngster) year at the Naval Academy
Began dating Barbara McKeldin in summer 1968, between John's third and fourth years at the Academy

1993: Alaska cruise with Barbara, her father and stepmother, and his mother Beryl and her husband Bob
As a small child John lived in Richmond and Sacramento, California, while his father worked for Union Oil after leaving the Army after WWII. (before 1952)
In 1952, when his father left for Okinawa, John, his mother and siblings lived in Pasco, Washington, near his mother's family until they could join him.
The family lived for almost two years in military housing in the town of Naha, Okinawa, with blackout shutters on the windows; John started school there. (1952 to about 1954)
John lived at the Presidio in San Francisco for his 1st through 4th grades (1954-1958), during his father's first assignment there.

On returning from Germany in 1962 (John's 9th grade), the family first lived in a flat in the Richmond District of San Francisco before getting housing on the Presidio, later in senior officers' quarters whose back yard was a fairway of the Presidio golf course.
John and Barbara arrived in Washington State in 1972.
After seven years in New Mexico, John and Barbara moved back to Ridgefield, WA (this passage gives his retirement as 2010; the summary chapter says 2009).

While living in Germany he toured France, Spain, Austria and Switzerland with his family, went to Great Britain with the Boy Scouts, and rode the trains through East Germany to the divided city of Berlin. (1960-1961)
The family came back to San Francisco in 1962 and lived on the Presidio until 1965, when he finished high school.
The family was living in Oak Harbor, Washington, in about 1973.
Before moving to New Mexico, John and Barbara lived in the 'blue house' in Ridgefield, Washington. (late 1990s)
Over the two years after the Rexam job ended, John drove a long-haul truck while still living in Vancouver, WA, and then moved to New Mexico for work. (about 2001-2003)
John and Barbara came back from New Mexico to the Vancouver area in January 2010 and settled in Ridgefield, WA, that year.
education: In high school John was a diver on the swim team, ran for class officer, was active in student government, played on at least three sports teams and belonged to a social club.

At the Naval Academy John played NCAA baseball and lightweight football for two years, boxed in the Plebe winter tournament, and with his handball partner reached the late rounds of the Brigade handball championship.
John earned his MBA at the University of Portland while working at a paper mill.

In high school (about 3,000 students, overlooking the Bay) he was class president twice (including senior class president), student body president, captain of several teams, a football and baseball player, MVP of his summer Babe Ruth baseball league, and prom king at his senior prom.
He earned his MBA at the University of Portland after about three years of part-time study begun roughly 14 years after his Naval Academy degree, while working at the Wauna Mill.
John earned his MBA by taking evening classes while he worked.
career: After 19 years with his first paper company, John took a management job with another paper company that was soon sold; he stayed in Redding working as a consultant, then became an Engineering Manager for another paper company in Vancouver, WA, which was also later sold. (about 1995-2000)
His first job was as a paperboy for the San Francisco Chronicle, which he kept until he left for Annapolis. (before June 1965)
On leaving active duty in 1976 he became a Mechanical Engineer with Crown Zellerbach Paper Company in Port Townsend, and he and Barbara bought their first home, on a hill overlooking the town.

In 1978 he took a fast-track management job with Crown Zellerbach's Containerboard Division and moved the family to Gilroy, California; when the promises weren't kept he moved back to the Paper Division.

He then took an engineering job at the Wauna Mill outside Clatskanie, Oregon, and the family lived in Kelso, Washington, for about 16 years; he later became Logistics Manager at Wauna and rose to Superintendent. The company went from Crown Zellerbach to James River to Fort Howard over those years. (c. 1979-1995)
In 1995 he left after 19 years to take a management job with Simpson Paper Company in Redding, California; six months later Simpson sold his division and the new owners let the managers go.

After Simpson he joined a consulting company teaching ways to improve human performance, and turned down an interview for a Mill Manager job in Michigan; over the next five years he held two more jobs, including long-haul trucking. (c. 1995-2000)
He drove long-haul truck for Swift in 2001 and accepted his State of New Mexico job over the phone while driving somewhere in Montana.

He worked for the New Mexico Public School Facilities Authority, managing state funding and overseeing construction and maintenance for over 50 public schools in west-central New Mexico, including the Navajo, Zuni and Acoma reservations, Grants, Gallup and Crownpoint, with his office in Crownpoint. (2000 or 2001-c. 2010)

John worked for James River Corporation in the paper industry; on a company visit to its St. Francisville paper mill near Baton Rouge he learned his one party trick, making two wine corks appear to pass through each other.

In 2001 John was Plant Engineer for the paper company Rexam in North Portland; when Rexam sold the plant to a competitor, his engineering job was cut and he managed the graveyard shift until the handover.

John and Barbara have 2 sons and 6 grandchildren. [Family research emails, email 49]
John and Barbara took an LDS genealogy class in March 2011 and researched at the Family History Library in April 2011. [Family research emails, email 37]
Unconfirmed: George believes John was likely named after their great-grandfather John Wesley Adams; John finds it dubious. [Family research emails, email 41]

Open question: Was George Francis I of Missouri the son of Joseph (an illegitimate son of JQ Adams) and Eliza Hamilton, or of Jose Pierre and Elizabeth, daughter of Francis and Susan Hamilton? George F. Adams and John Adams dispute Bill Allen's report [Family research emails, email 41]
Open question: John writes 'George and I live in WA' (email 49), but in email 41 he lives in Englewood, Colorado. [Family research emails, email 49, 41]
In school John was often team captain, class president or student body president, until he reached college. [John Howard Adams, A Memoir, text line 4372]

Since retiring, John and Barbara have travelled to Scotland, Ireland, continental Europe, Paris (three times), Normandy, a river cruise in France, Spain and Portugal, northern Italy, Switzerland, Norway, Finland, Australia, New Zealand, Alaska, the Caribbean, South America and the Falklands, Iguazu Falls, and Peru, Ecuador and the Galapagos. A planned Russia river cruise was cancelled four times, the last because of the war in Ukraine. [John Howard Adams, A Memoir, text line 3777]

CORRECTION 2026-09-23: The courtship began in summer 1968, not summer 1967: John met Barbara in 1967, when she was dating a classmate, and they began dating the following summer. [John Howard Adams, A Memoir, text line 1362, 1563]

Lowell Tiller, a Korean War Navy flight-crew veteran who hired him at Wauna, and his wife Lillian took the Adams family in almost as their own; Lowell was John's mentor and confidant. [John Howard Adams, A Memoir, text line 2140, 2144]

CORRECTION 2026-09-23: Joined the paper industry in 1976 (Crown Zellerbach, Port Townsend), not 1978, which was the move to Gilroy; and his New Mexico schools were in west-central, not north-central, New Mexico (Crownpoint, Grants, Gallup). [John Howard Adams, A Memoir, text line 2616, 2624, 2686, 2694]

Sources disagree on the engagement: John's record says the ring was presented in Nov 1968; Barbara writes that they first talked about marriage at the Army-Navy weekend at the end of Nov 1968 and went diamond shopping in Annapolis in Feb 1969. [Barbara McKeldin Adams, A Memoir, text line 1251]
The Alaska trip in the list of trips taken since retiring was earlier: Barbara dates their Alaska cruise to 1993.
